title: Sort machined blocks with a two-limit go/no-go gauge
instruction: Check each block, lying flat, with the two-bar gauge: put blocks that slide under the green GO bar but not under the red NO-GO bar in the green ACCEPT tray, blocks that don't fit under the GO bar in the red OVERSIZE tray, and blocks that also slide under the NO-GO bar in the blue UNDERSIZE tray.
context: Unlike a single-limit fit check, this needs both limits of a real two-limit gauge: every block is tried under the GO bar (is it oversize?) and then under the lower NO-GO bar (is it undersize?), and goes to one of three trays; gauging with either bar alone scores 0. Two-limit gauging is routine inspection on a machine-shop floor; the three heights are 3.5 mm apart, too close to judge reliably by eye.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y left; heights from the table top (74.75 cm above the floor); sizes are length (x) x width (y) x height. Blocks: six bare machined aluminium blocks (silver-grey), numbered on the underside, lying flat with the long side along x: 1, 6.4 x 4.4 x 3.20 (0.243 kg); 2, 6.0 x 4.2 x 3.55 (0.242 kg); 3, 5.4 x 4.1 x 3.90 (0.233 kg); 4, 5.6 x 4.1 x 3.90 (0.242 kg); 5, 5.6 x 4.0 x 3.20 (0.194 kg); 6, 5.5 x 4.0 x 3.55 (0.211 kg). Places: a front row at x = 10 and a back row at x = 17.5, each at y = 8, 0 and -8. Layouts (one per trial; block numbers by place, front row then back, left to right): A, 1 2 3 / 4 5 6; B, 2 3 1 / 5 6 4; C, 3 5 6 / 2 4 1. The screenshot shows A. Gauge: a fixed steel bridge, near face at x = 31, 2 cm deep; dark grey posts 2 x 2 cm at y = 12, 0 and -12; a green GO bar, 1 cm thick, from y = 1 to 13, underside 3.75 cm up; a red NO-GO bar from y = -13 to -1, underside 3.40 cm up; each over a 10 cm lane. Trays: fixed plastic, 1 cm walls 3 cm tall, 0.4 cm floor, centred at x = 30, 16 cm inside along x: a green ACCEPT tray at y = 18 to 36 inside; on the right one tray split by a 1 cm divider into a red OVERSIZE half (inside y = -15.5 to -26) and a blue UNDERSIZE half (inside y = -27 to -37.5).
scoring: Only the final sort is scored, not the gauge passes. In a tray (or half): centre inside its walls, underside within 1.5 cm of its floor (so not stacked or on a wall), still (under 1 cm/s), and both fingertip centres 2 cm or more from the block; any orientation. Right tray: ACCEPT for the 3.55 cm blocks (2 and 6: under GO, not under NO-GO), OVERSIZE for the 3.90 cm blocks (3 and 4), UNDERSIZE for the 3.20 cm blocks (1 and 5). Wrong: in any other tray, or off the table. Score, in order: 1.0 when all six are in their right trays (the trial ends once this holds 1 s); otherwise (right - 3 x wrong) / 6, not below 0, so 0, 1/6, ..., 5/6. Blocks anywhere else on the table, including one left under a bar, count neither way. So leaving everything, one tray for all, gauging with one bar (two blocks wrong) or swapping OVERSIZE and UNDERSIZE score 0; the best blind strategy expects 0.056. The task's score is the mean over one trial of each layout. On real arms, judge from a top-down photo after the arms withdraw, reading each block's number on its underside.
reset_notes: Put the six blocks back flat, long side along x, at the next layout's places (A, B, C in turn).
fidelity: Approximate. The limits are exaggerated: real gauges split hundredths of a millimetre; here the heights are 3.5 mm apart, a passing block clears its bar by 2 mm and a blocked one is 1.5 mm too tall, as tighter fits are unreliable in the simulator. The gauge and trays are fixed; three fixed layouts, chosen at the start. The blocks are rigid uniform boxes; the simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than bare aluminium on steel.
